newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada pledges to destroy most of its land mines.
newsitem.headline: Canada pledges to destroy most of its land mines.

text.p: Canada, on the eve of hosting an international conference aimed at a global ban on anti-personnel land mines, said on Wednesday it planned to destroy at least two-thirds of its stockpiles of the weapons.
Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy and Defense Minister David Collenette said Canada had already started eliminating its anti-personnel mines.
"By immediately removing two-thirds of our stocks, Canada has sent a powerful message to the world that we are committed to the eradication of these weapons," Collenette said in a news release.
Canada was hoping this week's conference would lead to global negotiations on the elimination of anti-personnel mines in 1997, Collenette said.
Canada now has a moratorium on the operational use, production and transfer of anti-personnel mines.

The three-day conference, which Axworthy called "a very significant landmark," is due to begin on Thursday with representatives of more than 70 governments, non-government organizations, international agencies and the United Nations expected to gather in Ottawa.
